questions.prompt: Which refactor scope should this goal cover first?
questions.description: Repo is a Rust CLI. Biggest concentration is src/cli.rs (~1836 lines), src/agents.rs (~1997), src/runner.rs (~2079), and tests/acceptance.rs (~3344).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Refactor whole codebase, but prioritize the large high-churn modules first: cli, agents, runner, acceptance tests. Leave tiny stable modules alone unless needed for clean boundaries.

options.label: Touch every module for consistent structure

questions.prompt: How strict should compatibility be while refactoring?
questions.description: Current CLI has stable dry-run output, explain JSON, mount/network/security refusals, image build behavior, and agent alias behavior covered by tests.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Strict compatibility: no intentional CLI, JSON, dry-run text, security policy, image build, or runtime behavior changes. Private Rust APIs may move/rename if tests and public behavior stay equivalent.

options.label: Allow small user-visible cleanups if documented

questions.prompt: What structure should the refactor move toward?
questions.description: Architecture docs currently prefer flat modules and warn against premature abstractions. This goal can introduce submodules where real domains already exist.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Extract domain-focused submodules without deep trait/plugin systems: CLI parsing vs plan building vs git metadata, agent aliases vs Pi state vs identity/socket mounts, runner execution vs copy/symlink filtering vs auth/proxy setup, acceptance tests split by behavior domain.

options.label: Split acceptance tests by behavior domain

questions.prompt: What testing bar should define success?
questions.description: Current suite has unit tests plus one large acceptance file. User request says preserve scenarios, refactor tests, and add missing ones.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Keep every existing scenario, split tests into domain files/helpers, add characterization tests before risky moves, add missing coverage for extracted boundaries, and require fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --locked, diff check, and key dry-run/explain smoke commands.

options.label: Add characterization tests before risky moves
Add missing unit/acceptance coverage for new boundaries

questions.prompt: What should be explicitly out of scope?
questions.description: Narrow out-of-scope choices reduce accidental feature work during broad refactor.
questions.recommendedAnswer: No new product features, no security-policy relaxations, no Docker image/toolchain changes beyond compile-required path updates, no public CLI/docs behavior changes except structure docs, no deep generic framework or plugin architecture.

options.label: No public CLI/docs behavior changes except structure docs
